source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check Mini DP can work with resolution change
1.Power on SUT and boot into OS.
2.Change the current video resolution and color depth to better.
3.Choose the "Test" button to test the changes, then choose "Apply" to accept the changes.
4.Shutdown and restart the OS, then login.
5.Review Event Viewer logs to confirm there are no errors or fault conditions reported.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1.All selectable changes up to 1920x1200 at a 16bit color depth should function properly. Higher resolutions may not work properly because of limitations of the video driver used and the supported resolutions of the monitor used.
2.Screen can display w/o error.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Resolution change up - 1920x1200x16bit: change the Mini-DP video resolution/color depth up to 1920x1200@16bit in the OS display settings. Requires a person at the display + OS desktop GUI (Test -> Apply); agent can read the current mode with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "xrandr 2>&1 | grep -iE 'connected|\*' | head 2>&1" if a GUI session is present, but the GUI change + visual confirmation are operator/visual.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the xrandr/DRM mode list so the user confirms 1920x1200@16bit applied properly on the Mini-DP display; the GUI apply + visual check are operator.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: resolution change is a GUI/visual check on the Mini-DP display - operator performs it; agent only reads the OS mode.

original_test_intent: Verify every owner-approved selectable MiniDP display mode through 1920x1200 at the source-defined 16-bit colour depth, including a visible error-free image, persistence through restart/login and clean Event Viewer/system logs.
original_method: An engineer uses the OS display GUI's Test and Apply actions for the approved mode matrix, visually validates the physical MiniDP display, shuts down/restarts and logs in, then reviews Event Viewer and supporting system/BMC logs.
manual_activity: The source requires GUI Test/Apply interaction and a human judgment that the physical screen displays without error. Restart/login and visual recovery also require an engineer even though mode and log collection can be assisted.
required_inputs: Exact OS edition/build and display GUI procedure
GPU/driver, MiniDP connector/cable and monitor/EDID identities
Definition of 16-bit colour and the complete selectable-mode matrix through 1920x1200
Maintenance approval, physical display operator and alternate console/revert path
safety_requirements: Do not apply an unadvertised or unapproved mode/depth or assume the output mapping.
Keep alternate KVM/console access and the previous known-good mode for recovery.
Treat shutdown/restart as service-impacting and preserve Event Viewer/system logs instead of clearing them.
Stop on blank/corrupt image, driver reset, failed login or inability to restore; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect OS-appropriate read-only GPU, connector, EDID, active mode/depth and log data before and after each approved change.
Track the approved mode matrix, restart timeline and operator evidence.
Compare logged errors and settings while leaving physical display quality and PASS/FAIL to the engineer.
engineer_actions: Approve the mode/depth matrix and recovery plan.
Perform GUI Test/Apply, visually inspect every required mode and conduct the approved restart/login.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not generally applicable. The source explicitly references Event Viewer and a GUI Test/Apply workflow, while xrandr is Linux-specific, read-only here and cannot prove colour depth or visible image quality.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use OS-native documented display inventory and event collection appropriate to the actual platform. Do not introduce a display-setting command until the OS/output/recovery plan is known.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All selectable modes through 1920x1200, 16-bit colour, Test/Apply, shutdown/restart/login, Event Viewer and 10/5-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: PLATFORM METHOD PENDING; RETAIN GUI/VISUAL CORE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Derive an explicit mode matrix from EDID and project acceptance, capture mode/depth before and after each GUI application, photograph a diagnostic pattern on the physical display, restart once after the final approved mode and export relevant display/driver events.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact OS, GPU/driver, MiniDP path and monitor.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record OS build, GPU driver/firmware and monitor EDID revision.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Owner display specification, OS vendor display-setting documentation and GPU/monitor supported-mode data.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds identity, matrix and evidence precision without replacing Test/Apply or visual observation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No lower selectable mode is omitted; no 16-bit support is inferred when the platform does not expose it.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: OS-specific definition and approved mode matrix.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A reported current mode cannot prove visual artifacts, colour-depth semantics or persistence by itself.

project_override_considerations: A project may define which advertised modes constitute 'all selectable' and clarify 16-bit semantics. If it approves fewer modes, completion applies only to that project plan and cannot claim the master matrix. Missing values are readiness inputs, not permanent BLOCKED.
expected_evidence: OS/GPU/driver/MiniDP/monitor/EDID identities and approved mode/depth matrix
Per-mode GUI Test/Apply result, electronic readback and timestamped visual evidence
Successful shutdown/restart/login with final mode retained
Event Viewer/system/BMC/SEL review, restored final state and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The procedure and criteria consistently require GUI application, physical display validation, restart and log review. The meaning/availability of 16-bit colour is a project readiness clarification rather than an internal contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The validation method is understandable. OS, EDID and colour-depth specifics determine execution readiness but do not permanently block the library case.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Reject generic xrandr as platform-neutral coverage and reject PARTIAL because visual GUI acceptance is core; retain readback as support only.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retain its display-stack, restart and recovery analysis while applying the locked MANUAL ONLY visual-core rule.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Preserves the all-selectable matrix and separates machine mode/log evidence from human image-quality acceptance.

review_improvement: Prevents one current-mode query from being reported as coverage of all selectable modes, 16-bit colour, visual quality, restart persistence and Event Viewer cleanliness.
independent_technical_reasoning: Automation can inventory modes and logs, but the source explicitly depends on GUI interaction and physical-screen observation for each mode. Those human acceptance signals make the case MANUAL ONLY rather than PARTIAL.
